ai.title: LLMs respond differently to harmful prompts when AI watermarking is used
ai.brief: SynthID can cause models to follow harmful instructions they would otherwise refuse. In response to a new European Union law, AI platforms are implementing new schemes for watermarking the content they generate. Anthropic recently disclosed its future Claude models will use SynthID-Text , an approach Google created and released as open source. It uses a secret key that subtly changes the process a model uses for choosing the next word in a sentence. ” Anyone who knows the key can determine if it was generated by the platform using it.

sec.title: RatHat Turns Android Accessibility Into an Attack Weapon
sec.brief: S. S. CISA adds Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog ENISA: Frontier AI Is Changing the Speed of Cyberattacks. Europe Needs to Catch Up RatHat is the new Android trojan you should know about. Zimperium researchers just published a breakdown of a strain they’ve traced to China-based operators, and what makes it different isn’t the credential theft, which is standard fare by now. It’s what it does to get there. It starts the way most mobile fraud does: a text message or a shady ad pointing to a fake app store. Once someone installs the APK, the malware doesn’t just ask for permissions and hope. “RatHat is primarily distributed through deceptive phishing sites promoted via malvertising, smishing campaigns, and third-party forums, luring victims into manually downloading malicious APKs that appear to be legitimate apps” reads the report published by Zimperium.
